title: 106. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Finding Constants of Inverse Proportionality
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Scaling One Variable in an Inverse Proportion
questions.learningObjective: Predict how one positive variable changes when the other is scaled in an inverse proportion.
questions.question: Two positive quantities are inversely proportional. If \(x\) is multiplied by \(3\), what must happen to \(y\)?
questions.explanation: For an inverse proportion, the product stays constant. Tripling one factor requires dividing the other by \(3\). Multiplying both by \(3\) would multiply their product by \(9\).
questions.hint: Identify what remains fixed when the two quantities vary inversely.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of inverse proportionality from a pair of values.
questions.question: If \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\), and \(y=8\) when \(x=5\), what is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: For inverse proportion, \(xy=k\). Substitute \(x=5\) and \(y=8\): \(5\times 8=40\). Therefore, the constant is \(40\). The alternative adds the values, \(5+8=13\), rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Check the product using a complete given pair.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of inverse proportionality from a table of values.
questions.question:
The table shows an inverse proportion between \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
x & 2 & 4 & 6\\
\hline
y & 12 & 6 & 4
\end{array}
\]
What is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: For an inverse proportion, the product \(xy\) is constant. Using the first column, \(2\times 12=24\). Checking the others, \(4\times 6=24\) and \(6\times 4=24\). Therefore, the constant is \(24\). The alternative copies a table entry, \(6\), instead of computing the constant product.
questions.hint: Consider how one factor must change to offset a change in the other.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of inverse proportionality in a fixed-journey speed-time context.
questions.question: The time \(t\text{ h}\) for a fixed journey is inversely proportional to the speed \(v\text{ km/h}\). When \(v=45\), \(t=4\). What is the constant of proportionality in \(vt=k\)?
questions.explanation: For inverse proportion, \(vt=k\). Substitute \(v=45\) and \(t=4\): \(45\times 4=180\), which is the journey distance in kilometres. The alternative divides the values, \(45\div 4=11.25\), rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Identify what remains fixed when the two quantities vary inversely.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of inverse proportionality from a pair of values.
questions.question: If \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\), and \(y=15\) when \(x=6\), what is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: For inverse proportion, \(xy=k\). Substitute \(x=6\) and \(y=15\): \(6\times 15=90\). Therefore, the constant is \(90\). The alternative adds the values, \(6+15=21\), rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Check the product using a complete given pair.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of inverse proportionality in a rectangle area context.
questions.question: A rectangle has a fixed area. Its length and width are inversely proportional. When the length is \(12\text{ cm}\), the width is \(5\text{ cm}\). What is the constant of inverse proportionality?
questions.explanation: For a fixed area, length and width satisfy \(\text{length}\times\text{width}=k\). Using the given values, \(12\times 5=60\). Therefore, the constant is \(60\). The alternative adds the side lengths, \(12+5=17\), then incorrectly labels that sum as an area. The constant product is \(60\text{ cm}^2\).
questions.hint: Identify what remains fixed when the length and the width vary inversely.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of inverse proportionality when the given values include fractions.
questions.question: If \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\), and \(y=\frac{2}{3}\) when \(x=18\), what is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: For inverse proportion, \(xy=k\). Substitute \(x=18\) and \(y=\frac{2}{3}\): \(18\times\frac{2}{3}=12\). The alternative divides \(18\) by \(\frac{2}{3}\), giving \(27\), rather than using the constant product.
questions.hint: Identify what remains fixed when the two quantities vary inversely.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of inverse proportionality from a point on the graph.
questions.question: The graph of an inverse proportion passes through the point \((3,14)\). What is the constant of proportionality in \(xy=k\)?
questions.explanation: A point \((x,y)\) on the graph satisfies \(xy=k\). Substitute \(x=3\) and \(y=14\): \(3\times 14=42\). Therefore, the constant is \(42\). The alternative adds the coordinates, \(3+14=17\), rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Check the product using a complete given pair.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate the constant of inverse proportionality when the given values include decimals.
questions.question: If \(y\) is inversely proportional to \(x\), and \(y=0.5\) when \(x=12\), what is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: For inverse proportion, \(xy=k\). Substitute \(x=12\) and \(y=0.5\): \(12\times 0.5=6\). Therefore, the constant is \(6\). The alternative divides \(12\) by \(0.5\), giving \(24\), rather than using the constant product.
questions.hint: Check the product using the complete given pair.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of inverse proportionality in a pump-time context.
questions.question: Nine identical pumps empty a tank in \(4\text{ h}\). The number of pumps \(n\) and the time \(t\) in hours are inversely proportional. What is the constant in \(nt=k\)?
questions.explanation: For inverse proportion, \(nt=k\). Substitute \(n=9\) and \(t=4\): \(9\times 4=36\) pump-hours. The alternative adds the values, \(9+4=13\), rather than multiplying.
questions.hint: Identify what remains fixed when the two quantities vary inversely.
